ideas.title: A bottom-bar quick-info widget, with one door anything can speak through
ideas.description:
Antonio, 2026-09-08, after seeing the refused-pick message land in the status bar: the bar should be a proper widget for short-lived information, styled, with a central API so a plugin or any component can put a line there.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT THIS
`AppState.status_note: Option<String>` — added with P082(F003)/T475. A pick with nothing to offer writes one sentence there, `chrome_status` (heca/src/chrome/theme.rs) appends it to the status text, and the next keypress clears it (heca/src/app/input.rs, at the top of `handle_keyboard_input`). It works and it is deliberately plain, but it is:

- **a string on `AppState`, not a widget.** The whole bar is one `Label` built from `format!("{pane_count} panes | {focus_title} | {mode_str}{tail}")`. There is no styling to give a message, no icon, no severity, no room for two things at once, and no way to draw the message differently from the pane count beside it.
- **host-private.** `state.status_note = Some(..)` is reachable only from inside the app. A plugin has no way to say anything there, and neither does a component that is not holding `&mut AppState`. That is the ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO failure: there is no line a plugin author could write.
- **one message, last writer wins.** Two things with something to say silently overwrite each other.

The toast stack was tried first and rejected by Antonio for this case: a key that could not do its thing is not an event worth covering the work with an overlay. So the two are not substitutes — a notification is an *event*, this is a *reply to what you just did*, and they want different surfaces. Whatever is built here must not become a second notification system; see the note on ownership below.

WHAT TO BUILD (to be designed, not decided here)
- A **widget** in `heca-grid-ui` for the bar's transient region: domain-neutral, theme-driven, able to show a short line with a severity and optionally an icon, and to fold to nothing when there is nothing to say (`Visibility` already does the folding — see the rule on its entry in docs/widgets.md).
- **One door to speak through**, reachable from all three surfaces AGENTS requires: the app, a plugin, and RPC. The test is the one in RULE ZERO — write the line a plugin author would type. If it needs a registry, an id, or a host-private type, the API is missing.
- **A lifetime rule stated once.** Today's is "until the next keypress", which suits a reply to a key. A message from a background job wants something else — a duration, or until it is replaced. Whatever the answer, it belongs to the widget or the door, never to each caller: a rule every caller has to remember is the bug.
- **What happens when two things speak at once** — a queue, a priority, or a refusal. Today the second silently wins.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING
- Is this the notification system's presentation for a `Toast`-unworthy severity, or a separate channel? Two systems that both put text on screen is exactly the "second path" AGENTS forbids — but a status reply and a notification genuinely differ in lifetime and in who dismisses them. Decide it explicitly rather than by which one gets built first.
- Does the bar keep its current fixed content (pane count | focus | mode) as segments, the way `[appearance.pane] title_segments` already configures the pane info bar? If so this is a segment kind, not a bolt-on, and the whole bar becomes configurable in the same breath.
- Who owns the bar's layout — is it a `ChromeRegion` with children, so a plugin could contribute a segment as well as a message?

WHERE THE CURRENT CODE IS
heca/src/chrome/theme.rs `chrome_status`; heca/src/app/render.rs `status_mode_parts`; heca/src/app_state.rs `status_note`; heca/src/app/input.rs (the clear); heca/src/handlers.rs `pick_refusal` (its first and only caller).

Once the door exists, `pick_refusal` should speak through it like anything else, and `status_note` should go.

ideas.title: A pane's actions and segments are a closed enum — nobody but the host can add one
ideas.description:
Raised by Antonio 2026-09-22 while deciding the region API (P082(F003)/T518). Leave the code as it is for now; this records what is wrong and the shape agreed for the fix.

THE DEFECT
`PaneAction` (Split, MoveLeft, MoveRight, Close, Zoom, Float) and `PaneSegment` (Location, AppName, PaneName, GitBranch, …) are closed Rust enums in `heca-config/src/appearance.rs`. `config.toml` picks from that list BY NAME, which reads like an open vocabulary and is not: a plugin cannot add an action or a segment at all, because there is no variant for it. Adding one means editing the host and recompiling it.

The pane header consumes them in `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs` — `content.actions` is `&[PaneAction]`, and `pane_action_spec` maps each variant to a glyph, a `WmAction`, a label and a focus rule.

WHY IT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS REGIONS
A fixed list the host owns, selected from by name, with no way for anyone else to contribute. That is exactly what T518 removes for a chrome region. Antonio, 2026-09-22: a plugin or another developer should add a pane action the way a provider is added to a sidebar —

    pane_actions::append(..).prepend(..).remove(..).retain(..)

and the same for segments. Internally that checks what `config.toml` asked for and builds the keys and ids itself, so no caller composes one.

THE ORDER, DECIDED
T518 (the region API) lands first and this reuses its shape — a handle fetched by name, `append`/`prepend`/`remove`/`retain`, placement and `.order` carried by the child, no index methods. Building this before T518 would write the same mechanism twice.

WHAT IT TOUCHES
- `heca-config/src/appearance.rs` — the two enums stop being the vocabulary. A configured name becomes a name, resolved against what was contributed.
- `heca/src/chrome/pane_header.rs` — `pane_action_spec`'s match is one contributor among others, not the whole list.
- The identity work in T474: an action's widget key is composed from the pane it belongs to plus the action's name, so a contributed action gets a correct key without its author knowing the rule.

⚠️ Not a licence to start. Propose the task and agree it when T518 is done.

ideas.title: heca-ide — nvim-engine IDE in a heca pane (styled GUI + classic-keybinding layer)
ideas.description:
## The ask (Antonio, 2026-10-21)
A keyboard-first IDE heca hosts in a pane: full **vim/nvim** power, but able to **switch to classic (non-vim) keybindings** like Zed. Must be **expandable with no base-code ceiling** — add vim-class features (quickfix, fzf, DAP, hover, completion…) without hitting "the base won't let you." The GUI must be **beautiful** (nvim's built-ins work but are unstyled; we draw our own).

## Decision (Antonio, 2026-10-21): nvim as the engine, heca as the GUI
Use **embedded Neovim as the editor engine** — not Zed, not Lapce, not a from-scratch editor. Why: nvim already has, with **no base ceiling because it *is* nvim**, the whole feature set — LSP client (completion/hover/signature/diagnostics/code-actions/rename/inlay-hints), tree-sitter, **nvim-dap** debugging, quickfix/loclist (core), fzf/telescope, Lua + remote plugins. A native editor (Lapce/Zed) would mean rebuilding all of that ourselves. This extends heca's existing **F007 nvim-GUI** work into an IDE.

## How it works
- **Engine:** `nvim --embed` headless; heca attaches as a **GUI client** over msgpack-RPC (crate `nvim-rs`; heca already plans `rmpv`). nvim does all editing + plugins.
- **Beautiful GUI via UI externalization:** `nvim_ui_attach` with `ext_multigrid` + `ext_linegrid` + `ext_hlstate` + `ext_popupmenu` + `ext_cmdline` + `ext_messages` + `ext_tabline`. nvim then sends **structured data** (not drawn cells); heca renders the grid, completion menu, cmdline, messages, tabs with **heca-grid-ui + its text renderer** — styled, not nvim's plain TUI.
- **Rich LSP UI (what `ext_popupmenu` can't give):** a thin **nvim-side Lua → RPC bridge** forwards structured `vim.lsp` results (completion kinds/docs, hover markdown, signature params, diagnostics) to heca; heca draws native VSCode-style cards. ext_* for chrome, the bridge for rich content.
- **Panels** (problems/quickfix, references, call stack/variables, breadcrumbs): data from nvim (LSP / nvim-dap / quickfix), UI = heca chrome around the pane.
- **Classic (non-vim) keybindings — NOT `set insertmode`** (that guts undo granularity, jumps, operators, registers). Instead a **command-mapped layer**: classic gestures → nvim's *real* commands (Ctrl+Z→undo tree, Shift+arrows→visual select, Ctrl+C/X/V→registers, Ctrl+S→:w, Ctrl+F→search, goto→LSP). The buffer never leaves nvim's model, so undo/jumps/LSP/plugins stay intact. Implemented as a **toggleable nvim Lua keymap profile** (nvim = single source of truth) — "vim off" like Zed, inverse implementation. **This translation layer is the genuinely hard/finicky part** (reference: VSCode-Neovim, where mode-sync bugs cluster).

## Governing rule
**nvim owns the engine + all data (LSP/DAP/plugins — one source of truth); heca owns the pixels.** Nothing is "unsupported": heca either draws nvim's version (cheap) or draws its own from nvim's structured data (polished). Never run a second LSP/parser in heca — it would drift.

## Build path
Bootstrap **A** (attach + render grid + ext_* externalized UI as nvim produces it → everything works, drawn by us), then upgrade pieces to **B** (heca-drawn from the LSP bridge) for VSCode-grade polish. We implement no LSP/DAP ourselves.

## Synergy with F012
nvim's UI protocol natively supports **multiple UIs per instance + detach/attach** (`:detach!`, `--remote-ui`) → maps onto heca's F012 detach/attach and several-windows-per-session (several UIs on one nvim = several windows editing one session).

## References
- **Neovide** (Rust, GPU, MIT) — reference GPU nvim GUI; attach + grid/ext handling; uses `nvim-rs`.
- **nvui** — richly styled external popupmenu (colors/icons/borders).
- **zonvie / goneovim** (akiyosi; Zig / Go) — UX reference for which elements to externalize + message routing / tabline styles.
- **neovim-qt** — externalized popupmenu. Spec: `:help api-ui-events` / `ui.txt` (the ext_* event protocol heca implements).

## Rejected alternatives (kept for the record)
- **Native editor from Lapce** (Apache-2.0; `lapce-core`/`lapce-proxy`/`lapce-rpc`, verified UI-free at manifest level) or **Helix** (`helix-core`, MPL-2.0, terminal/modal). Rejected vs nvim: would mean rebuilding quickfix/dap/fzf/LSP/plugins ourselves; nvim gives them free. Lapce's `wasmtime` WASI plugin host may still inform heca's own WASM runtime (F003/P022).
- **Zed** — rejected: GPL-3.0, and GPUI owns its own window (can't live in heca's wgpu compositor).

## Scope
Large; promote to a feature + phases when started. Near-term editor stays the current F007 nvim-GUI work; heca-ide is that taken further.
